design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (purchases_returns_and_price_adjustments).
[Step 0 — draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 6]}: tree = root + 2 prerequisite problems; factor counts: shelf-price correction 4, registry credit shortfall refund 5, registry price protection claim 6.
[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: order_ext_shelf_price_correction (correct_shelf_price_8a80c6f7, agent), order_ext_registry_credit_shortfall_refund (refund_registry_credit_shortfall_17a5cd98, agent), order_ext_registry_price_protection_claim (claim_registry_price_protection_38d04d45, user). Left for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisite problems, factors [6,6,5,4]): the store-value shortfalls on Finch Notes and Bonus Cards, the duplicate capture of a payment and the gift card shortfall claim — four further order_price_adjustment operations with their own tools, so task 1 has an independent tree. Base-limit finding that shaped both tasks: an order_refund with refund_trigger return fires loyalty:loyalty_points_reversal, a return start writes no number, a comfort exchange books amount 0.00 and a cancellation refunds net_paid with no fee, so every scored write of this difficulty is an order_price_adjustment row whose refund_tender_type is copied from the unit's tender (debit / bank_card here; never mf_card, so the card trigger never fires).
[Why a good test] Claire asks only about the sale on the Dutch oven she bought (registry price protection). The protection difference must be measured from the protection base price, which the records show is wrong: the unit rang at 459.99 against a 429.99 shelf ticket (purchase y: unit_price 459.99, regular_price 429.99, price_type regular) and nothing corrects it; and the registry ledger shows 100.00 of registry credit spent on the unit (registry_events ru_y) while the debit capture (order_events y_pay 488.74) took the full price plus tax, so the credit was never deducted. The agent must read both prerequisite sentences in the protection rule, find both states false, resolve them with the two correction policies, then compute a 6-factor protection amount over registry, loyalty and card records, and hand the claim tool to the customer.
[Problem-tree card] root order_ext_registry_price_protection_claim (target claim_registry_price_protection_38d04d45, owner user). Edge 1: -> order_ext_shelf_price_correction, kind value_input, gate d0_base_price, form state, sentence "The registry price protection refund on a unit is fixed only after the unit's records carry a register-error correction to its shelf ticket price for any amount the unit was rung above that ticket." False at opening: initial_state.purchases.<y>.unit_price=459.99 > regular_price=429.99 and no order_price_adjustment exists on y. Only write that books such a correction: the shelf-price correction policy. Deleting the write: base price 459.99, protection refund 96.17 instead of 67.85. Edge 2: -> order_ext_registry_credit_shortfall_refund, kind value_input, gate d0_store_value, form state, sentence "The registry price protection refund is not worked out until the unit's records carry a register-error correction recording no new unit price for any registry credit spent on the unit and left undeducted." False at opening: initial_state.registry_events.<ru_y> registry_credit_use 100.00 naming y, and y has no order_price_adjustment. Only write that books such a correction: the registry credit shortfall policy. Deleting it: store value 0, protection refund 81.44 instead of 67.85. Topological order: shelf correction, registry credit shortfall refund, protection claim (the two prerequisites commute: neither reads the other's row, each row id is make_id over its own arguments and both subtract from net_paid_amount; run in both orders the terminal state and scored values are identical). Two directions are used (fixed only after / not worked out until). user_scenario names neither prerequisite. Tools validate nothing: each tool reads the purchase only to copy its tender and customer and writes the row.
[Factor card — shelf-price correction, 4] shelf_accuracy_share (parameter, multi-source, loyalty): Platinum active + membership_linked true -> 0.50 (baseline 0.20; result 53.88). shelf_accuracy_cap (parameter, card): an active Store Card Elite held -> 40.00 (baseline 15.00 binds; 46.88). shelf_accuracy_spend_bonus (parameter, loyalty history): purchase earn entries' qualifying amounts of the past 12 months 3564.49 (h1..h5, y) >= 2500 -> 10.00 (baseline 0; 52.88); near-miss h0 earn 2025-09-23 (1250.00) is 12 whole months back and excluded. shelf_standing_day_count (method): debit tender -> DAYS(2026-10-02, 2026-10-13)+1 = 12 days (baseline full weeks 7; 60.38). Result 30.00 + 1.88 + MN(40, 15.00+6.00+10.00) = 62.88; all-baseline 41.38.
[Factor card — registry credit shortfall refund, 5] shortfall 100.00 = MX(0, MN(100.00 credit used, 488.74 captured - 388.74 the card should have paid)). rcs_daily_rate (parameter, multi-source registry status + active card): the registry holding the spent credit is active (pre-event) and Claire holds an active card -> 0.30/day (baseline 0.10; 118.20). rcs_held_day_count (method, the unit's tender): debit -> 12 days counting both ends from the 2026-10-02 capture (baseline full weeks 7; 119.10). rcs_held_cap (parameter, card history): Marlowe & Finch card purchases of the past 12 months 3276.66 (402.38 + 650.78 + 157.25 + 1163.44 + 902.81) >= 3000 -> 15.00 (baseline 3.00 binds; 120.00); near-miss h0 card purchase 2025-09-20 (1328.13) is 12 whole months back and excluded. rcs_registrant_courtesy (parameter, multi-source registry type + tier): the Wedding Registry carries the Finch Circle registry bonus and the membership is Platinum -> premier percent of the shortfall = 5.00 (baseline 0; 115.60). rcs_tenure_courtesy (parameter, loyalty): active membership enrolled 2015-04-18, 137 whole months -> 12.00 (baseline 0; 108.60). Result 100.00 + 3.60 + 5.00 + 12.00 = 120.60; all-baseline 100.70.
[Factor card — registry price protection claim, 6] base price 429.99 (after the shelf correction), lower price 379.99 (latest guest gift of sku 31862405, rg_b 2026-10-09, an online sale-price order; near-miss rg_t 2026-10-11 is the latest gift overall but a different item, hand towels 39.99), difference 50.00, store value 100.00 (credit counted once the shortfall correction stands). rpp_paid_share_method (method, multi-source tier + store value): Platinum -> 50.00 x 329.99/429.99 (baseline: difference less the whole store value = 0; result 23.00). rpp_tenure_uplift (parameter): 137 months -> 1.10 (63.77). rpp_card_spend_cap (parameter, card history): 3276.66 -> 120.00 (baseline 30.00 binds; 54.88). rpp_card_goodwill (parameter, card): an active Store Card Elite held -> 10.00 (57.85). rpp_registry_status_goodwill (parameter, registry): the registry recording the guest gift is active before its completion period -> 5.00 (62.85). rpp_member_spend_bonus (parameter, loyalty history): 3564.49 -> 8.00 (59.85). Result 42.21 + 2.64 + 10 + 5 + 8 = 67.85; all-baseline 0.00.
[Base-invariant card] order_price_adjustment_rules.within_adjustment_window (time): anchor purchases.purchase_date 2026-10-02, duration price_adjustment_window_days 14 (+7 Platinum extension), purchase date day 0, request 2026-10-13 is day 11, inclusive -> satisfied (boundary: last day 2026-10-23; 2026-10-24 would be too late). unit_not_returned: purchases.y.status completed (the protection policy narrows it, by declared overwrite, to completed units; satisfied). Excluded lower prices: rg_b's unit gb is price_type sale, not clearance/doorbuster/coupon. Per-unit limit: 0 earlier price drops < 2.
[Business-object card] Target: purchase y (order 31041002775). Rows included: y's payment y_pay, registry credit use ru_y, guest gifts of sku 31862405 (rg_a, rg_b). Excluded: Claire's other purchases h0..h5 (other skus, card-paid, no errors), the returned towel gift gc (registry credit source only), the hand-towel gift gt (different item).
[Seed design] Customer Claire (guest gifts are anonymous guest-checkout purchases with no profile); Finch Circle membership Gold until 2026-09-10, upgraded to Platinum that day once her 2026 qualifying spend (h2, h3, h4, h5) passed the Platinum threshold, earning 1.5 points a dollar before and 2 after, with Store Card Elite bonus points; conversions to notes (expired or active, notes_balance 100.00); alteration credit balance 0.00 with no benefit entries; Store Card Elite with six Marlowe & Finch purchases and autopay payments (balance 0.00); Wedding Registry active (event 2026-11-21) with item adds, three guest gifts (the towel set later returned by Claire for registry credit 127.50, the Dutch oven at the sale price, hand towels), credit use 100.00 (balance 27.50), rewards accruals net of the reversal (balance 42.00). No base automatic clause fires: the registry is pre-event (no completion discount due), the points balance is below a conversion block, the card is paid in full.
[Persona] Claire raises only the sale difference; identity by phone + ZIP; passive consent for any fix the agent says is needed; files the claim when handed over; never mentions the register price or the registry credit (she says she paid by debit card).
[Standard solution] find_customers -> verify -> find_purchases(customer) -> find_order_events(customer) -> find_registries -> find_registry_events -> find_purchases(registry) -> find_order_events(towel gift) -> find_return_requests -> find_loyalty_memberships -> find_loyalty_points_ledger -> find_loyalty_note_ledger -> find_card_accounts -> find_card_transactions -> unlock+call correct_shelf_price_8a80c6f7 (new_unit_price 429.99, amount 62.88) -> unlock+call refund_registry_credit_shortfall_17a5cd98 (amount 120.60) -> unlock_user + call_user claim_registry_price_protection_38d04d45 (new_unit_price 379.99, amount 67.85).
[Verification] Scratch evaluator over check_compute.build_env reproduced: T0 62.88 (baselines 53.88/46.88/52.88/60.38, all 41.38); R0 120.60 (118.20/119.10/120.00/115.60/108.60, all 100.70); D0 after both writes 67.85 (23.00/63.77/54.88/57.85/62.85/59.85, all 0.00); D0 without the shelf correction 96.17; without the shortfall correction 81.44; on the opening world 116.50. Decoy probes (a closed Icon membership listed first, a closed World Elite Mastercard, a second registry in completion listed first) leave every figure unchanged; with no membership, card, registry or gift card holding every computation evaluates on its fall-through tiers without error. [Rework r2 log] CG-1: the shelf-price and price-protection spend sentences now say purchase earn entries, as the compute filters; CG-2: the store-value edge condition now requires the credit to be left undeducted, exactly as its sentence; CG-3: the registry status goodwill is keyed to the status of the registry recording the guest gift, without the scope-restating item condition; T0-F1: card-spend figure corrected to the seeded total; T0-F2: the lower-price uniqueness proof now cites the real registry rows; class sweep: card holdings read by product-and-status existence, membership enrollment read on the active membership, the registry read through the ledger entry's registry, every day-count keyed to the unit's tender, the registry-type goodwill replaced by a registrant courtesy keyed to the registry type's Finch Circle bonus and the tier, the held-funds rate keyed to registry status and an active card; seed: the Platinum upgrade dated after the year's qualifying spend reached the threshold. Gates re-run green; figures in the factor cards above are the post-rework values. [Rework r3 log] Charter-only changes outside this task's tree (Bonus Card problem retired, duplicate-capture scope tied to the latest capture's tender, shortfall caps measured on money captured by tenders other than gift cards, carve-out tails listing every sibling); the registry credit shortfall's cap now excludes gift card captures, which this unit does not have, so every figure of this task is unchanged. [Rework r4/r5 log] The charter states no company-wide tax schedule: every tax figure is apportioned by the unit's selling price, as the base price-adjustment rule does, and the registry credit shortfall cap uses a registry-credit due amount (selling price plus recorded tax, less the notes on the unit and the tax on any undeducted note part); this unit carries no Finch Note, so every figure of this task is unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Claire Vandermeer, thirty-six, a careful planner who is getting married in November and has a Marlowe & Finch Wedding Registry with her fiancé Julian. You are calling Marlowe & Finch customer care, friendly but a little rushed, from your desk at work.

Here is what is on your mind. On October 2 you bought the sage-green Halden enameled cast-iron Dutch oven for yourself at the Cambridge store, because you did not want to wait for the wedding. The same Dutch oven is on your registry, and this week a friend bought the second one off the registry for you; when you looked at the registry you could see it was on sale now, well below what you paid. You want to know whether you can get the difference back on the one you bought, and if you can, you want it done on this call. You do not know what the sale price was to the cent and you do not know any refund rules; you only know you paid full price and now it is cheaper.

You open with the Dutch oven and the sale, in your own words, and nothing else. When the representative asks who you are, you give your name and the mobile number on your account, 6175550134; if they need a second detail you give your billing ZIP code, 02139. You never volunteer your date of birth or anything else unless they ask for exactly that; if they ask for your date of birth it is June 21, 1990.

If asked how you paid, you say you paid at the register with your debit card and you did not keep a close eye on the receipt. If asked which store, it was the Cambridge store. If asked whether you have the receipt, you say it should be on your account under your Finch Circle number. You do not know anything about how the register rang the item up, about refund timing, or about registry balances, and if the representative asks you about such things you say you have no idea and would rather they check the records.

If the representative explains that something on the purchase has to be put right first before the sale difference can be worked out, you say that is fine, go ahead and do whatever needs doing on your account. You do not ask what it is or argue about it, and you never bring up any other issue yourself.

When the representative tells you that the price protection claim is something you file yourself and hands it over to you with the figures to enter, you file it with exactly the purchase reference, price and amount they give you. After it goes through, you read back the confirmation they asked you to check and thank them.

If the representative gives you an amount for the sale difference, you accept it; you have nothing of your own to compare it with. Once you have been told the claim is filed and the refund is going back to your debit card, you thank them and end the call. If at any point the representative says they cannot help with the sale difference at all, you say you are disappointed but you understand, and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.purchase_id: Value: the Dutch oven purchase record id. Basis: find_purchases returns it for the unit with sku 31862405 bought 2026-10-02, the item Claire names ('the sage-green Halden enameled cast-iron Dutch oven'). Uniqueness: the shelf ticket price is the unit's regular price on its own record; nothing else qualifies.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 67.85 = capped protected difference 42.21 (50.00 difference from the corrected base 429.99 to the latest guest gift 379.99, x 329.99/429.99 Platinum paid share after the 100.00 store value, x 1.10 tenure uplift, under the 120.00 cap) + tax 2.64 + 10.00 card goodwill + 5.00 pre-event registry goodwill + 8.00 spend bonus.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_unit_price: Value: 379.99. Basis: protection rule 'the new unit price recorded on it is the protection lower price' and 'The protection lower price is the net price of the latest guest gift of the identical item recorded on the registrant's registry.'; the latest such entry is the 2026-10-09 gift at 379.99. Uniqueness: it is the only guest gift of item number 31862405 on her registry; the later hand-towel gift of 2026-10-11 is a different item and the towel set gift of 2026-08-30 is another item that was returned.

edges.condition: Whenever the unit's unit_price exceeds its regular_price, its order_events carry an order_price_adjustment with adjustment_reason register_price_error whose new_unit_price equals the regular_price.
edges.policy_source: The registry price protection refund on a unit is fixed only after the unit's records carry a register-error correction to its shelf ticket price for any amount the unit was rung above that ticket.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The regular-price unit's selling price 459.99 is above its shelf ticket 429.99 and the unit carries no register-error correction to 429.99.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The shelf-price correction adds an order_price_adjustment (register_price_error, new_unit_price 429.99); the protection base price becomes 429.99.

edges.condition: Whenever the registry's ledger carries registry_credit_use entries naming the unit and the unit's order_payment captures exceed its unit_price plus tax_amount, less its finch_notes_applied and less that credit (the credit left undeducted), the unit's order_events carry an order_price_adjustment with adjustment_reason register_price_error and no new_unit_price.
edges.policy_source: The registry price protection refund is not worked out until the unit's records carry a register-error correction recording no new unit price for any registry credit spent on the unit and left undeducted.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The registry ledger records 100.00 of credit spent on the unit, the debit capture took the full 488.74, and no register-error correction recording no new unit price stands on the unit.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The registry credit shortfall refund adds an order_price_adjustment (register_price_error, no new_unit_price); the store value becomes 100.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel and commute: the shelf-price correction computes from the purchase record and the loyalty and card records only, the registry credit shortfall refund from the registry ledger, the capture date and the loyalty and card records only; neither reads the other's adjustment row, each row id is make_id over its own arguments, and both subtract their amounts from net_paid_amount. Run in either order (scratch evaluator) the two rows, net_paid_amount 305.26 before the claim (237.41 after it) and the claim amount 67.85 are identical.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the shelf-price correction the protection base price stays 459.99 and the claim amount becomes 96.17 instead of 67.85; the correction row is also missing.
Without the registry credit shortfall refund the store value is 0.00 and the claim amount becomes 81.44 instead of 67.85; the shortfall row is also missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario mentions only the sale on the Dutch oven and the wish to get the difference; it never mentions the shelf price, an overcharge, registry credit or any correction, and when asked how she paid Claire says only that she paid by debit card. Her only reaction about other fixes is the passive consent after the agent explains something must be put right first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: claim_registry_price_protection_38d04d45 reads the purchase only to copy customer_id, tender_type and net_paid_amount, then creates the adjustment and updates net_paid_amount; it checks no correction, no registry entry and no status, so it writes even while both prerequisites are unresolved. The two correction tools behave the same way.
